variants.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Produce ONE complete refined spacecraft DESIGN SHEET, titled "L66 / R1". This is a coherent evolution of the WHOLE L66 ship: hull, shoulder transitions, engine seating, tail, equipment and wing accommodation. A beautiful functional Freelancer Liberty pirate fighter. This is NOT a tail-only variation and NOT a rear-view-only picture.

REFERENCE ROLES:
Image 1 is L66. Its UPPER-RIGHT REAR 3/4 has the best overall design and is the primary construction reference: broad faceted fuselage, two horizontally separated compact engines, integrated central stern rising into a substantial TWO-SECTION mechanical tail, useful equipment planes. Evolve that WHOLE ship into a more elegant connected design. Its upper-left front view has a contradictory tail orientation: do not copy that tail. The rear shape governs all new views.
Image 2 is the immutable actual li_pir_elite cockpit AND open three-rib collar: preserve capsule size, shape, glazing boundaries, shell, frames, neck and three angular ribs. No canopy enlargement or new brow.
Image 3 gives the ordinary THREE separate Defender fan-wing leaves and original root: blue front, green middle, amber rear. Preserve all three full plates and three distinct free tips per side, recolored native pirate red. Preserve their emergence at the LOWER FRONT CORNER of the MAIN HULL after the short neck behind the collar. No hinge on the collar, roof or engine. This native wing overrides L66's two-leaf proposal. Keep one native equipment plate on the rear leaf, not one on every leaf.

ONE INTEGRATED WHOLE-SHIP IMPROVEMENT:
Keep the recognizable elongated polygonal main body and overall L66 proportions. Re-sculpt its outer hull into coherent two-level shoulder surfaces: a short chamfered front shoulder begins BEHIND the open collar, a long shallow inset waist sits above the original wing roots, and the upper shoulder broadens subtly toward the engine supports. This must visibly improve the body silhouette in front, side AND rear; don't merely change the tail and texture.
The lower side is a purposeful recessed channel accommodating the three folding plates. Give it depth, an angled upper boundary and a closed inner backing, rather than loose decorative armor strips. Keep the actual wing-root point unchanged.
Seat both engines partly into angular aft shoulder recesses, with a SHORT visible structural collar around each engine body. Refine their housings into tapered polygonal forms, slightly narrower aft, clearly attached to the same hull planes. Two exhausts remain fully separate and unobstructed. Avoid bulbous glued-on pods, long pylons or extra engine. Keep upper motor covers free of equipment.
The central stern ramp, between engines, grows continuously into the lower tail section. Preserve L66 REAR's two overlapping substantial tail sections, approximately its original height/mass, ordinary equipment mounting flats, short blunt upper end and clear nesting seam. The surrounding hull shoulders and tail ramp share deliberate diagonal lines, so the ENTIRE ship reads as one designed machine. No broad pedestal or stack of tiers; no tiny triangular plaque/fin. Tail upper mass points toward the COCKPIT.
The roof stays closed and fairly flat, with restrained flush native paired baydoors ahead of the tail root. No central trench, raised twin walls, oversized hatch frame or tail footing crossing the doors.

ART DECO / EMPIRE:
Express these through the proportions and rhythm of stepped frame edges, a carefully framed long side relief field following the new shoulder angle, subtle fan/ray relief tied to the collar's existing motif, and sparse parallel ribs integrated into structural transitions. The shallow decoration belongs to actual hull fields. It must not turn into a cathedral, palace ornament, carved tombstone or sculptural statue. Keep functional metal, native warm red-brown/ochre exterior, blue glazing, slightly darker recesses. Calm readable panel surfaces with restrained seams and wear; avoid cracked stone/brick texture, excessive rivets, open pipes, framework, skulls or spiky villain styling.

CRITICAL MULTIVIEW CONSISTENCY:
Every drawing on this sheet has the NOSE POINTING RIGHT. Consequently upper tail mass leans UP-RIGHT toward the cockpit in EVERY perspective and SIDE. Rear 3/4: exhausts near LEFT, cockpit far RIGHT, as in original L66 rear. Front 3/4: cockpit near RIGHT, stern receding LEFT. Do not use a nose-left front view. TOP also has cockpit RIGHT. Keep same shoulder geometry, engine seating, substantial two-section tail, tail direction, three wing leaves, collar proportions and aft root in every panel.

PRESENTATION:
Landscape full design sheet on neutral light grey. Two equally useful LARGE views across upper two-thirds: FRONT 3/4 and REAR 3/4, both full-ship, same visual scale. Lower row: clear SIDE FLIGHT, TOP, and smaller SIDE STOWED. Show all three original wings nested back/inward along the lower hull in stowed view; tail sections only nest slightly and remain substantial. Full ship visible with margins, no cropped tips, no vignette hiding silhouette. Crisp believable industrial concept rendering with designed large and medium geometry, not a texture-only reskin. Labels just "L66 / R1", "FRONT 3/4", "REAR 3/4", "SIDE FLIGHT", "TOP", "SIDE STOWED". No prose, callout clutter, extra ships or alternate designs.
